text:
maria: Quick thread — proposal for who owns what telemetry in the onboarding pipeline. TL;DR: bench team keeps golden inputs & quality evals; runtime/infra owns ingestion metrics, latency, and alerting. vote or concerns?

derek: +1 to split, but we need a clear contract. What exact metrics cross the boundary?

sangeeta: We should list the metrics and their SLAs. My proposal:
- bench: per-model quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-drift/acceptance-rate)
- infra: p99 latency, qps, cold-start rate, kv-cache hit rate, OOMs

leo: Also add "smoke_pass" boolean from preflight (bench->infra) so infra can route. bench says whether model passed lightweight smoke.

maria: Exactly. smoke_pass is an explicit field in the manifest. infra uses it for fastpath routing.

 tom: How about telemetry ownership for golden regressions? If bench sees a regression during prebench, do they own the alerting lifecycle or does infra?

sangeeta: Bench should own regression triage + gold update decisions. Infra owns operational alerts (pager if latency spike, error rates). So bench triggers a ticket with reproducer, infra triages ops incidents.

maria: Proposed minimal contract (manifest keys + telemetry hooks):
manifest: { model_id: string, smoke_pass: bool, golden_sha: string, golden_inputs_uri: s3://..., prebench_stats_uri: s3://..., bench_owner: @sangeeta }

derek: We need a push pattern for prebench_stats (bench -> infra). Maybe an event to topic `onboard.prebench.v1` with payload = manifest + stats. infra subscribes and stores in tsdb.

leo: +1. Also add sample_size and seqlen_hist to that payload so infra can pick right kernel.

admit-bot: SYSTEM: prebench event schema version v1 accepted.

maria: For alerts: define two classes:
- Quality alerts (bench): triggered when delta on quality metric > threshold over golden. Create PR + triage ticket.
- Operational alerts (infra): triggered on p99>slat, OOMs, cache miss storms. Pager on sev 1.

 tom: Question: where to store golden inputs? If bench owns them but infra needs read access at runtime for replay, permissions become important.

sangeeta: Keep golden inputs in a read-only bucket with cross-account IAM role for infra. bench rotates golden_sha and writes manifest update. infra reads golden_inputs_uri only when running replays.

maria: Implementation plan in 2 sprints:
Sprint 1: define event schema, add smoke_pass to manifest, set up topic + tsdb mapping, infra read-only role, docs.
Sprint 2: alert wiring: bench quality alert -> ticketing integration; infra ops alerts -> pager and runbooks.

leo: Can we add a lightweight runbook snippet here? e.g., runbook check for p99 spikes:
1. check tsdb: `select p99 from onboard_latency where model_id=X last 15m`
2. check kv-cache hit: `kv_hit / kv_lookups`
3. if cache miss > 20% and p99 > SLA => scale pool or fallback to small-llm pool

maria: Good. Also add a guardrail: if bench quality drops after a release, autoscale should NOT be used to hide quality regressions. Must prefer fallback routing to older model variant.

derek: Agree. Add explicit fallback policy in manifest: `fallback_model_id` with semantics.

admit-bot: NOTE: new manifest field `fallback_model_id` required for dedicated deployments.

sangeeta: One more ops-y question: how do we surface golden drift to product owners? Bench can create weekly digest with top 5 drifts and signal owners.

maria: Yeah put that in Redwood Console under model -> onboard -> weekly regressions. Bench owns the digest.

tom: Any objections to the plan? If not I'll make an RFC PR that lists the schema and sprint plan.

sangeeta: No objections. Please add seqlen_hist and sample_size to the event schema.

derek: +1. Also add explicit retention policy for prebench_stats (90 days) and for golden inputs (indefinite but versioned).

maria: Thanks all. @tom assigned to RFC. I'll create the manifest template in the bench repo and link here. :rocket:
